title: Optimizing and Securing the Application knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Optimizing and Securing the Application”?
options: Optimizing and Securing the Application should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Optimizing and Securing the Application helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Optimizing and Securing the Application means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Optimizing and Securing the Application removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Optimizing and Securing the Application helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Optimizing and Securing the Application is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Bundle and rendering optimization” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Bundle and rendering optimization” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Bundle and rendering optimization” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Bundle and rendering optimization” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Bundle and rendering optimization” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Bundle and rendering optimization” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Bundle and rendering optimization” under Optimizing and Securing the Application. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Optimizing and Securing the Application”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
